introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Physics 2 (0780), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2020. Time allowed: two and a half hours.**

Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour, Section II in 30 minutes and Section III in 1 hour. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you must show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators and formulae booklet are allowed.

**Structure of the paper.** SECTION I (One hour, answer all questions): questions 1 to 5 are compulsory; in question 6 answer EITHER 6 (a), (b) and (c) OR 6 (d), (e) and (f). SECTION II (30 minutes): DATA ANALYSIS, question 7. SECTION III (1 hour): OPTIONS - answer any two questions from the four options (Option 1: Energy resources and environmental physics, question 8; Option 2: Communication, question 9; Option 3: Electronics, question 10; Option 4: Medical physics, question 11).

No data sheet is printed in the paper: whenever a constant is needed, the model answer states the value it uses.

questions.enonce_markdown:
*Figure 10* shows a photovoltaic plate used to light a bulb in a certain household.

![fig-1](gce-al-physics-2020-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_8_fig_1.png)

The solar panel has a power output of $50.0\ \mathrm{W}$.

(i) If the efficiency of the panel is $30\ \%$, determine the power input into the photovoltaic plate.

(ii) Above the earth's atmosphere, the solar constant is $1.4\ \mathrm{kW\,m^{-2}}$. However, only $40\ \%$ of this power per unit area reaches the earth. Estimate the surface area of the panel in figure 10.

(iii) Explain why solar energy is referred to as a renewable source of energy. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Power input.** $\text{efficiency} = \dfrac{\text{power output}}{\text{power input}}$, so
$$P_{\text{in}} = \frac{P_{\text{out}}}{\eta} = \frac{50.0}{0.30} = 167\ \mathrm{W}$$

**(ii) Area of the panel.** Intensity of sunlight reaching the ground: $0.40\times1.4\ \mathrm{kW\,m^{-2}} = 0.56\ \mathrm{kW\,m^{-2}} = 560\ \mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$. The panel must collect $167\ \mathrm{W}$, so (assuming the panel faces the Sun squarely)
$$A = \frac{P_{\text{in}}}{I} = \frac{167}{560} = 0.30\ \mathrm{m^{2}}$$
**Area $\approx 0.30\ \mathrm{m^{2}}$.**

**(iii) Renewable.** Solar energy comes from nuclear fusion in the Sun, which will continue to radiate for billions of years; the energy is **continuously replenished by nature** and is **not used up** when we use it, unlike fossil fuels which take millions of years to form and are consumed faster than they are replaced.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) What is the ozone layer?

(ii) Name a substance which is responsible for the depletion of the ozone layer and explain how this substance contributes to the depletion of the ozone layer.

(iii) State two effects of the depletion of the ozone layer on life on earth. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) The ozone layer** is a region of the **stratosphere** (roughly 15 to 35 km above the Earth's surface) where the concentration of **ozone**, $\mathrm{O_3}$, is relatively high. It **absorbs most of the harmful ultraviolet radiation** (especially UV-B and UV-C) coming from the Sun.

**(ii) Substance and mechanism.** **Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)**, formerly used in refrigerators, air conditioners and aerosol sprays, are the best-known cause.

- In the stratosphere, ultraviolet radiation breaks a C-Cl bond and releases free chlorine atoms: $\mathrm{CFCl_3 \xrightarrow{UV} CFCl_2 + Cl}$.
- A chlorine atom destroys ozone: $\mathrm{Cl + O_3 \to ClO + O_2}$.
- The chlorine is then regenerated: $\mathrm{ClO + O \to Cl + O_2}$.

Chlorine acts as a **catalyst**: it is not used up, so a single chlorine atom can destroy many thousands of ozone molecules. The ozone layer therefore thins (the "ozone hole" over Antarctica). Other substances: halons, nitrogen oxides, methyl bromide.

**(iii) Two effects of the depletion** (more UV reaches the ground):

- more cases of **skin cancer**, sunburn and **cataracts** (eye damage), and a weakened immune system in humans ;
- damage to **plants and crops** (lower yields) and to **plankton** in the oceans, which disturbs food chains ; also damage to materials such as plastics.
